The cgroup pidlist rework in 2.6.32 generates the BUG_ON
when pidlist_array_load() calls cgroup_pidlist_find():
(1) if a matching cgroup_pidlist is found
column2: it down_write's the mutex of the

column1: pre-existing cgroup_pidlist
(2) if no matching cgroup_pidlist is found
column2: then a new one is allocated

column1: down_write's its mutex
column2: and the use_count is set to 0.

column1: (3) the matching
column3: cgroup_pidlist gets returned back to pidlist_array_load()

column1: which increments its use_count -- regardless whether new or pre-existing --
and up_write's the mutex.
So if a matching list is ever encountered by cgroup_pidlist_find() during
the life of a cgroup directory
column2: it results in an inflated use_count value

column1: preventing it from ever getting released by cgroup_release_pid_array().
Then if the directory is subsequently removed
BUG_ON() when it finds that the directory's cgroup is still populated with
a pidlist.
The patch simply removes the use_count increment when a matching pidlist
is found by cgroup_pidlist_find()
column2: because it gets bumped by the calling

column1: pidlist_array_load() function while still protected by the list's mutex.
